effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the message, data structure and signature sections of the LOGOS-SERVICE-DISCOVERY specification named in the context, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ that fails on the audited commit for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Scope of this audit: the messages, data structures and signatures, and the protocol's entry module. Trace the requirements of the spec's sections 'Data Structures' (Advertisement, Ticket), 'System Parameters' (the defaults), 'RPC Messages' (base message structure, advertisement encoding, the REGISTER and GET_ADS requests and responses, the encoding and field rules of Message Validation, advertisement signature verification, Stream Management), the definitions 'Service ID', 'Address', 'Signature' and 'Expiry Time E', and 'Client and Server Mode'. The rest of the spec is staged as reference; do not trace it. Three sibling audits cover the registrar, the advertiser and the discoverer; how each role acts on a decoded message is theirs, not this audit's.

nim-libp2p is the Nim implementation of libp2p; the Logos service discovery protocol lives in libp2p/protocols/service_discovery.nim and libp2p/protocols/service_discovery/. This unit is service_discovery.nim (the entry module: setup, modes, the maintenance heartbeat), types.nim (messages, tickets, system parameters and their defaults, encode/decode), connection.nim (streams, read limits), dial_backoff.nim and libp2p/extended_peer_record.nim (the signed advertisement and its envelope domain and payload type). The role files (registrar.nim, advertiser.nim, discoverer.nim), the Kademlia code in libp2p/protocols/kademlia (including the message type numbers in protobuf.nim) and the generic signed-envelope code are outside the unit: read them where a requirement leads there, and mark behaviour that lives only there 'not in unit'. The C bindings in cbind/ are out of scope. Record the resolved commit in the report.

The spec's 'Example ... algorithm' sections, the Appendix and the Implementation Notes other than Client and Server Mode are illustrative or recommended; a different algorithm that meets the normative MUST/SHOULD text is not by itself a divergence. Treat code comments that cite the spec as claims to check.

Running tests: tests are Nim unittest files named test_*.nim; tests/test_all.nim imports every test_*.nim under tests/ whose path contains the -d:path substring, so `make test service_discovery` compiles and runs everything under tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ (unit tests there, multi-node tests in component/, shared helpers in utils.nim). The gate puts nim 2.2.14 from /w/cache/nim-2.2.14/bin on PATH and runs `make test service_discovery`. Do not use nix: the flake's dev shell ships a nimble too old for the Makefile. New proof tests go in tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ as their own test_*.nim file named by finding id, are picked up with no other edit, and should copy the header and import style of an existing file there (SPDX header, `{.used.}`, the unittest wrapper from tests/tools/unittest). The build uses --styleCheck:error, so follow the existing naming. No external network is available to tests; a proof that needs a live remote peer is 'needs external evidence'.
